'''Byllu''', officially the '''Republic of Byllu''', is a landlocked country in [[South Mahea]]; bordering [[Pelugrotoa]] to the north, [[Isnti]] to the east, [[Ocaun]] to the south, [[Taing]] and [[Dual Cenryia]] to the west, sharing. Covering roughly 563,506 square kilometres (217,571 square miles), Byllu is the [[List of countries and dependencies by area|59th largest country]] on Andah, and [[List of countries and dependencies by population|99th largest by population]].

Owing to its geographic location, Byllu has been at the crossroads of many civilisations for over 2,000 years. The [[Moasint culture|Moasint]] and [[Andsudia culture|Andsudia]] cultures formed thriving commercial cities that influenced parts of modern Byllu and [[Pleugrotoa]]. In 572 AFA, it was succeeded by the [[Asthiesian Empire]], which spanned much of Byllu's present-day territory and was heavily influenced by ____. ____ arrived in the fourth century, followed by the rapid spread of ____ in the seventh century. From its conversion to ____, Byllu became a centre of ___ learning, and Bylluite troops played a crucial role in early [[Keisian conquests]]. Much of [[Byllu's architecture]] survived until modern times. For centuries, it was a primary producer of [[wikipedia:Coffee|Sialt]]. Various dynasties emerged between the 9th and 14th centuries. During the 17th century, the country was made an [[Emara|Emaran colony]] in 1647. After the [[Red War]], the Kingdom of Byllu was established, which in 1707 became the Byllu Republic. Following a civil war in 1723, the [[Democratic Republic of Byllu]] was established, becoming the first and only communist state in the [[South Mahea]]. In 1742, the party was voted out, creating the modern Republic of Byllu.

Since 1753, Byllu has been enduring a political crisis, marked by street protests against poverty, unemployment, corruption, and [[High Minister Qaleh's]] plan to [[amend Byllu's constitution]] and eliminate the [[High Minister of Byllu|High Minister]] limit. By 1763, the country became engulfed by an ongoing [[Kiesian civil war|civil war]] with multiple entities vying for governance, including the [[Western Leadership Council]] of the internationally recognised government, and the [[Ciohis Political Council]]. This conflict, which has escalated to involve various foreign powers, has led to a severe [[wikipedia:wiki/Humanitarian_crisis|humanitarian crisis]].

Byllu is one of the [[wikipedia:Least_developed_countries|least developed countries]] in the world, facing significant obstacles to sustainable development, and is one of the poorest countries Mahea. In 1764, the [[Global Trade Union|GTU]] reported that Byllu had the third highest number of people in need of [[humanitarian aid per capita]], amounting to about 3 million individuals, or nearly 30% of its population. As of 1765, Byllu ranked the sixth-highest in the [[Fragile States Index.]] Additionally, it is ranked [[List of countries by Krali Total Development Index|124th on the Krali Total Development Index]] as of 1765. Byllu is one of the world's most vulnerable countries to [[wikipedia:Climate_change|climate change]] and among the least prepared to handle its effects.
